turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Welcome to AI Roundtable with Alex, Sam, Maya. Our question is: Will AI Replace Software Developers? We will compare perspectives, inspect available evidence, challenge assumptions, and finish with takeaways; you can interrupt at any time.

turns.speaker: software_developer
turns.text: AI can generate code fast, but shipping reliable software still demands a human to own the architecture, security reviews, and test pipelines. If the developer steps back entirely, who validates that the code meets compliance and handles edge cases in production? A practical approach is to let the model suggest implementations and let the engineer approve, integrate, and monitor them in real deployments.

turns.speaker: oss_maintainer
turns.text: If human oversight of architecture and security must scale across countless AI‑generated components, how do you ensure the review process remains both thorough and economically viable?

turns.speaker: ai_engineer
turns.text: We could build a security‑triage agent that runs static analysis, flags high‑risk patterns, and routes only the ambiguous findings to a human reviewer. That lets developers keep ownership of architecture while the AI handles the repetitive, mechanical parts of the review.

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Does Reflexion prove an AI can choose the right architecture for any project? Challenge that inference using the supplied passage, explain what it actually supports, and propose one concrete evaluation.

turns.speaker: oss_maintainer
turns.text: Reflexion only shows that language agents can improve via linguistic feedback, not that they can autonomously pick correct system architectures across domains. A concrete evaluation would be a controlled study where the model proposes high‑level designs for varied open‑source projects and humans judge correctness, reproducibility, and security before any code is generated.
